title: When the Lights Go Out
content:
Mia had recently moved into an old apartment in the center of town. The building was quiet, and the rent was surprisingly cheap. At first, she thought she had found the perfect place.

On her first night, however, something strange happened.

Mia was reading in the living room when the lamp beside her suddenly went out.

She looked at the bulb.

— That's strange.

She turned it on again. The light worked normally.

A few minutes later, it went out again.

Mia replaced the bulb and continued reading.

At midnight, she went to the kitchen to get some water. As she entered the hallway, the kitchen light suddenly went out.

Then the bathroom light went out.

Then the bedroom light.

One after another, the lamps in the apartment were turning off by themselves.

Mia froze.

— Okay... this isn't normal.

She checked the electrical panel, but everything seemed fine. She turned the lights back on and returned to the living room.

For several minutes, nothing happened.

Then the lamp beside her went out again.

This time, Mia heard something.

A soft sound came from the hallway.

Tap.

Tap.

Tap.

She stood up slowly.

— Is someone there?

There was no answer.

Mia walked toward the hallway. As she moved, the lights began to turn off again.

One.

Two.

Three.

She stopped.

At the end of the hallway, a dark figure seemed to be standing near the bedroom door.

Mia immediately turned on her phone's flashlight.

There was nobody there.

She looked around nervously.

— I'm just tired. That's all.

She decided to sleep in the living room with the lights on.

At around three in the morning, she woke up.

The apartment was completely dark.

Her phone was next to her, but before she could reach for it, the lamp above her suddenly turned on.

For a moment, Mia felt relieved.

Then she noticed something written on the wall.

DON'T TURN OFF THE LIGHTS.

She stared at the message.

— I didn't write that.

The lamp went out.

Mia grabbed her phone and turned on the flashlight.

The message had disappeared.

Then she heard the sound again.

Tap.

Tap.

Tap.

It was coming from behind her.

She slowly turned around.

A woman was standing in the corner of the room.

She was wearing an old white dress, and her face was almost impossible to see.

Mia couldn't move.

The woman raised one hand and pointed toward the hallway.

Every lamp in the apartment suddenly turned on at the same time.

Then they all went out.

Mia screamed.

When she opened her eyes again, the room was empty.

The next morning, Mia called the building manager.

— Has anything strange ever happened in apartment 304?

The manager became silent.

— Why do you ask?

— The lights keep turning off by themselves.

The man's face changed.

— You should move out.

— Why?

He looked at the floor.

— A woman lived there many years ago. She died during a power failure. The lights went out just before they found her.

Mia felt a cold shiver.

— What happened to her?

The manager looked toward the hallway.

— Nobody knows. But since then, the lights in that apartment have sometimes turned off by themselves.

That evening, Mia packed her bags.

Before leaving, she looked back at the apartment one last time.

Every light was on.

She smiled nervously and reached for the door.

Then the hallway light went out.

And from inside the dark apartment, she heard a woman's voice whisper:

— Don't leave me alone.
